investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (peer-pod VM slots exhausted or not allocatable), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 122–146 seconds across all three checks, the agent creation workflow never progressed past pod scheduling, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing a full contract validation failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval run.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots on those nodes are currently allocated to other workloads, leaving no capacity for a new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free a slot.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector targets only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes happen to be at capacity. If the selector was recently broadened or narrowed (e.g., by a node label change or a pod spec change), the effective eligible node set may have shrunk.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pod workloads (out of 6 total), and concurrent remote-agent demand has saturated those 2 nodes simultaneously across all three eval checks.

QUATERNARY — Node health degradation: one or both kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may be in a degraded state (e.g., NotReady, MemoryPressure, or the kata-agent daemonset is unhealthy), causing the extended resource to report zero allocatable capacity even if no pods are actively consuming it.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (peer-pod VM slots exhausted or not allocatable), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 122–146 seconds across all three checks, the agent creation workflow never progressed past pod scheduling, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing a full contract validation failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 18:52 and 18:57 UTC on 2026-07-13 with identical Kubernetes Unschedulable errors reporting that 0/6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-runtime eval produced zero evidence — all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted by the remote-agent eval probes remained Unschedulable for the full timeout window (~122–150 s), preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence collection to fail. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion localized to the remote-agent scheduling path; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader production incident is present in the packet.
